templates.name: BIND9 DNS (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for ansible/playbooks/bind9/bind9-dns.yml. Copied from zabbix_template_proxmox.json's own generator and expanded, 2026-10-20, following a shopping-list-first review of the full 1588-line playbook (both Play 1 and Play 2).

*** DOES NOT STANDALONE-IMPORT *** -- this template deliberately does NOT declare nodeinfo.json's master item (vfs.file.contents[...]) or its 15-field base schema, which every OTHER template in this series (linuxtools, ansible-node, firewall, cloudpanel, proxmox) currently DOES independently re-declare. Zabbix does not allow two items with the same key on the same host, even from different templates -- found while building this one: the moment any host has linuxtools AND a role-specific template BOTH linked (the normal, intended case, since every host gets linux/tools.yml plus its own role playbook), that's a real conflict. This template's own 4 nodeinfo_extra items (section G below) are DEPENDENT items referencing linuxtools' own master key by name. REAL LIVE FINDING, 2026-10-24: the earlier assumption here (that this would just resolve once a host had both templates linked) was wrong -- configuration.import rejected a standalone import of THIS template with "Incorrect value for field master_itemid: ... not found", because resolving a cross-template master item needs an explicit parent-template declaration on THIS template object, not just co-presence on a future host. Fixed by adding a top-level "templates" (linked/parent template) entry referencing linuxtools_examplemusic by its technical name -- unverified against a real re-import as of this note, flagged for confirmation on the next attempt. The other 4 templates' own exposure to this same conflict is NOT fixed here -- Robert's own call to defer the full fix to a later backlog item (consolidating everything into linuxtools with preprocessing-based placeholder values for fields that don't apply to a given host).

SECTIONS
  Packages (7): bind9/bind9utils/arping/iproute2/network-manager/bc/localepurge, deduped against common_packages (vim/curl/tmux/grc/zsh/zsh-autosuggestions/zsh-syntax-highlighting/bind9-dnsutils already checked by linuxtools).
  Listeners: net.udp.listen[53] (local LISTEN-state check -- confirmed there is no net.udp.port key at all, net.tcp.port's UDP equivalent takes no ip parameter) + net.tcp.port[,53] (BIND also listens TCP for transfers/large responses). Both lightweight/local, 10m delay.
  Functional DNS test: the native net.dns/net.dns.record key family (a real dedicated Zabbix agent item type for exactly this, not a hand-rolled dig via system.run) -- forward (A) and PTR lookups against 127.0.0.1, mirroring bind9-dns.yml's own existing Section 9 self-test. Both the success/fail boolean AND the actual resolved value (compared against {$DNS.OWN_IP}/{$DNS.OWN_HOSTNAME}) are checked -- a real correctness test, not just 'did it respond'. 1h delay, per explicit instruction not to hammer the server.
  Config/zones: named.conf.options/local (written on BOTH master and slave, confirmed directly -- only the zone-file writes below are role-gated) via a content-regexp matching the file's own managed-by comment. The 3 fixed zone files (forward/provisioning-reverse/CLD-LAN-reverse) are MASTER-ONLY ({$DNS.ROLE}="master"). The per-site reverse-zone loop (57+ sites, too many to enumerate individually) uses the same count-comparison 'box clever' pattern as the proxmox template's own pools check -- sites.csv rows (minus CLD) vs real db.192.168.* files (minus the 2 fixed ones) -- for the same reason (no process substitution under system.run's POSIX sh). Same documented limitation: doesn't name which site, tolerates extras.
  Scripts: reloadbind/checkbind (world-readable, 0755) get exists+cksum, same pattern as proxmox -- but these are INLINE YAML content blocks, not standalone files, so their cksum was computed by actually parsing bind9-dns.yml's own real YAML (not retyping it) and rendering the one genuine Jinja substitution (domain), then cross-checked byte-for-byte against an independently hand-typed copy. Would need updating if the domain is ever renamed. editzone (0750 root:root) is exists-only -- content unreadable by an unprivileged zabbix-agent user; Robert's own call, not worth adding zabbix-agent to the root group just for one checksum.
  Network: prov-static.nmconnection, exists-only (0600 root:root, same pattern as cloudpanel/proxmox).
  nodeinfo.json extras: dns_ip/zone/zone_serial/interface -- see the template's own top-level note above for why these are the ONLY nodeinfo-related items declared here.

{$DNS.ROLE} scopes which triggers are meaningful for master-only checks -- real concrete example, not hypothetical: EXADNSVRK001 is the master, EXADNSFRD001 is the slave/secondary (confirmed directly from configs/inventory/{vrk,frd}.ini and this playbook's own README).

NOT YET LIVE-IMPORTED OR LIVE-TESTED against a real Zabbix server or a real zabbix-agent -- same status as every other template in this series.

IMPORT: configuration.import, rules: createMissing+updateExisting+deleteMissing on items/triggers, createMissing+updateExisting on template_groups/templates.

items.name: named listening on UDP/53
items.description: 1 if UDP port 53 is in LISTEN state (local socket inspection, not a network probe -- net.udp.listen has no ip parameter at all, unlike net.tcp.port).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - named is not listening on UDP/53
triggers.description: UDP/53 isn't in LISTEN state. Check named is running (systemctl status named).

items.name: named listening on TCP/53
items.description: 1 if a TCP connection to port 53 succeeds -- BIND also listens on TCP (zone transfers, large/truncated responses), not just UDP.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - named is not listening on TCP/53
triggers.description: TCP/53 isn't accepting connections. Check named is running (systemctl status named).

items.name: DNS self-test: forward lookup resolves
items.description: 1 if named resolves {$DNS.OWN_FQDN} (A record) via its own loopback -- mirrors bind9-dns.yml's own Section 9 self-test.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - DNS forward self-test failed
triggers.description: named did not resolve {$DNS.OWN_FQDN} at all. Check named-checkconf / journalctl -u named. If this is a slave ({$DNS.ROLE}), check the real master is reachable -- a transient master outage self-heals once AXFR completes.

items.name: DNS self-test: forward lookup value
items.description: The actual resolved A record for {$DNS.OWN_FQDN} -- compared against {$DNS.OWN_IP} for a real correctness check, not just 'did it respond'.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - DNS forward self-test resolved the wrong IP
triggers.description: named resolved {$DNS.OWN_FQDN} to something other than {$DNS.OWN_IP} -- zone data is wrong, not just unreachable.

items.name: DNS self-test: PTR lookup resolves
items.description: 1 if named resolves {$DNS.OWN_PTR_NAME} (PTR record for this host's own IP) via its own loopback -- mirrors bind9-dns.yml's own Section 9 self-test.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - DNS PTR self-test failed
triggers.description: named did not resolve {$DNS.OWN_PTR_NAME} at all. Check named-checkconf / journalctl -u named. If this is a slave ({$DNS.ROLE}), check the real master is reachable.

items.name: DNS self-test: PTR lookup value
items.description: The actual resolved PTR value for {$DNS.OWN_PTR_NAME} -- checked for containing {$DNS.OWN_HOSTNAME} (substring, matching bind9-dns.yml's own Section 9 'in' check -- a PTR value carries the full FQDN plus a trailing dot, not a bare hostname).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - DNS PTR self-test resolved the wrong name
triggers.description: named's PTR answer for {$DNS.OWN_PTR_NAME} doesn't contain {$DNS.OWN_HOSTNAME} -- zone data is wrong, not just unreachable.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - named.conf.options is missing or not Ansible-managed
triggers.description: Re-run bind9-dns.yml -- see its 'Write named.conf.options' task.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing /etc/bind/db.{$DNS.DOMAIN} (forward zone)

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing /etc/bind/db.192.168.69 (CLD LAN reverse zone)

items.name: Per-site reverse zones: expected count (sites.csv rows minus CLD)
items.description: Number of sites.csv rows excluding CLD -- one per-site reverse zone file is expected per site (bind9-dns.yml's own per-site loop, rejectattr Site==CLD).

items.name: Per-site reverse zones: actual count (real files, excluding the 2 fixed ones)
items.description: Number of real /etc/bind/db.192.168.* files, excluding the provisioning (139) and CLD LAN (69) reverse zones already checked individually above.

triggers.expression: {$DNS.ROLE}="master" and last(/BIND9 DNS (Example Music)/system.run[ls /etc/bind/db.192.168.* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE "db\.192\.168\.(139|69)$" | wc -l,wait])<last(/BIND9 DNS (Example Music)/system.run[tail -n +2 /etc/example-music/sites.csv | grep -v '^CLD,' | wc -l,wait])
triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - fewer per-site reverse zones than sites.csv rows
triggers.description: Fewer per-site reverse zone files exist than sites.csv has non-CLD rows -- a site was added but its reverse zone hasn't been (re)generated yet. Re-run bind9-dns.yml --tags zones-full,reload against the master. Count comparison only -- doesn't identify WHICH site, and deliberately tolerates MORE files than sites (a renamed/retired site's old zone file surviving isn't itself a fault).

items.name: File exists: /usr/local/bin/editzone
items.description: 1 if /usr/local/bin/editzone exists. EXISTS-ONLY, no cksum -- mode 0750 owner/group root means an unprivileged zabbix-agent user can't read its contents at all (stat for existence works fine regardless, since that only needs directory traversal on /usr/local/bin/, not permission on the file itself). Robert's own call: leave it exists-only rather than adding zabbix-agent to the root group just for a checksum.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing /usr/local/bin/editzone
triggers.description: Re-run bind9-dns.yml.

items.name: File exists: prov-static NetworkManager profile
items.description: 1 if the prov-static .nmconnection profile exists. Mode 0600 root:root (confirmed directly in bind9-dns.yml's own template task) -- exists-only, same pattern as cloudpanel/proxmox's own NetworkManager profile checks.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing the prov-static NetworkManager profile
triggers.description: Re-run bind9-dns.yml.

items.name: nodeinfo.json contents, bind9 extras (master)
items.description: Raw nodeinfo.json content -- master item for this template's own 4 bind9-specific examplemusic.nodeinfo.* dependent items below (dns_ip/zone/zone_serial/interface). Deliberately a SEPARATE item from linuxtools_examplemusic's own vfs.file.contents[/etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json] master (same file, read twice -- negligible cost, a local file read), NOT a cross-template DEPENDENT reference to it -- the original templates:[linuxtools_examplemusic] parent-link this template had is REMOVED, 2026-10-29 (Robert's sweep, fixing the same bug class as proxmox/cloudpanel): Zabbix refuses to link a template declaring another as its parent to any host that ALSO links that parent directly, which is every host here. Same fix as firewall_examplemusic/proxmox_examplemusic's own master item of this shape -- see feedback_zabbix_duplicate_item_keys_across_templates.md for the full finding. The UTF-8 encoding param exists purely to give this item a distinct key from linuxtools' own bare-key item. No staleness trigger of its own -- linuxtools' own master item's nodata() trigger already covers this same file going stale, one alert, not duplicated here.

items.name: nodeinfo: dns_ip (bind9-specific)

Master item (vfs.file.contents[/etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json]) is deliberately NOT declared in this template -- see this template's own top-level description for why.

macros.description: Whether this host is the BIND9 master or a slave/secondary (bind9-dns.yml's own dns_role variable). Valid values: "master" or "slave". Real example, not hypothetical: EXADNSVRK001=master (default), EXADNSFRD001=slave -- set this macro to "slave" on that host's own linked template.
The zone this server is authoritative for (bind9-dns.yml's own domain variable, derived from benarbejde/ad_forest.json). Used to build the forward zone's file path.
This host's own lowercase hostname (zone records are deliberately lowercase, standard DNS convention). Default is EXADNSVRK001's -- override to exadnsfrd001 on that host.
This host's own FQDN, queried for the forward self-test. Default is EXADNSVRK001's -- override to exadnsfrd001.jukebox.internal on that host.

This host's own real IP (confirmed from configs/inventory/vrk.ini), compared against the forward self-test's resolved value. Default is EXADNSVRK001's -- override to 172.16.124.8 (EXADNSFRD001, confirmed from configs/inventory/frd.ini) on that host.

The in-addr.arpa name for this host's own IP, queried for the PTR self-test. Default is EXADNSVRK001's (192.168.139.8 reversed) -- override to 8.124.16.172.in-addr.arpa (EXADNSFRD001, 172.16.124.8 reversed) on that host.

Expected cksum of /usr/local/bin/reloadbind's rendered content (domain=jukebox.internal substituted, computed by parsing bind9-dns.yml's own real YAML). Update this macro's value if that script's content, or the domain itself, ever changes.

Expected cksum of /usr/local/bin/checkbind's rendered content (domain=jukebox.internal substituted, computed by parsing bind9-dns.yml's own real YAML). Update this macro's value if that script's content, or the domain itself, ever changes.

Item-key namespace prefix for every examplemusic.nodeinfo.* dependent item in this template series. Was hardcoded as a literal string in ~74 item keys across 7 templates -- Robert's explicit ask (2026-10-16 design brief: "macros wherever sensible"), 2026-10-25: a single macro here instead, so this repo's own harness can find/verify/change the one real source of truth per template instead of grepping scattered literals.
